title: Percy Fawcett
subtitle: The Lost City of Z · Mato Grosso, Brazil, 1925
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the dense tropical rainforest and slow brown rivers of Mato Grosso, Brazil, in the mid-1920s, humid green-grey light, period 1920s expedition gear, melancholy and uncanny, cinematic vertical composition with one centred subject, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Mato Grosso, Brazil, nineteen twenty-five. Percy Fawcett, his son Jack and Raleigh Rimell went into the forest, looking for a lost city he called Z.
beats.img: An old brass explorer's compass resting open on a folded, weathered canvas map case on a rough wooden supply crate, centred and well lit by warm late-afternoon sun, a wall of dense tropical rainforest softly out of focus behind, no writing visible, no people.

beats.vo: He had left word. If they did not return, no one should come looking.
beats.img: A narrow footpath leading straight into a dense green tropical rainforest, centred, the trail vanishing into deep shadow between giant tree trunks and hanging vines, shafts of hazy light, still and silent, no people.

beats.vo: On May twenty-ninth, he wrote to his wife from Dead Horse Camp. You need have no fear of any failure.
beats.img: A single folded sheet of old paper covered in faint illegible handwriting, no readable words, beside a fountain pen on a worn canvas camp table in a small jungle clearing, centred, lit by a glowing oil lantern at dusk, hammock ropes and dark forest behind, no people.

beats.vo: It was the last word from any of them. None of the three was ever found.
beats.img: An abandoned jungle campsite at dawn, centred, a cold fire ring of stones, an empty canvas hammock slung between two trees, mist drifting through dense rainforest, quiet and deserted, no people.

beats.vo: Searchers went in anyway. Later, bones were said to be his. Scientists in London found they were not.
beats.img: A wide slow brown river bend at dusk between unbroken walls of dark tropical rainforest, centred, mist on the water, a pale fading sky, vast and unresolved, no boats, no people.

facts.claim: In 1925 Percy Fawcett set out into Mato Grosso, Brazil (from Cuiabá) with his son Jack and Jack's friend Raleigh Rimell, seeking a lost city he called 'Z'
Fawcett left instructions that if the expedition did not return, no rescue should be sent
His last letter, to his wife (Nina), was dated 29 May 1925 from Dead Horse Camp and included the line 'You need have no fear of any failure'
That letter was the last communication from the party; none of the three was ever found
Search expeditions followed regardless (Dyott 1928 first; many later)

Bones obtained by Orlando Villas-Bôas (1951) were presented as Fawcett's; the Royal Anthropological Institute in London examined them (Cave report 24 Oct 1951) and found conclusively they were not his
Still unsolved as of 2026: History.com (updated 3 Sep 2026) says the cause of the disappearance remains a mystery; 2025 centenary coverage reports no new evidence
